what: 4a. Step-by-step, once you decide to go for it
title: Releasing CodeCarbonR
text: Pre-submission (addition package-specific fixes ): Every exported function (setup_carbon_tracker(), carbon_tracker(), with_emissions_tracked(), list_carbon_tracker_countries(), carbon_tracker_ready()) needs @examples block roxygen comment. Added 2026-08-19. One correction plan originally written: list_carbon_tracker_countries() actually call ensure_codecarbon_available() internally, (unlike carbon_tracker_ready(), genuinely safe unwrapped) needed \donttest{} , unwrapped example. setup_carbon_tracker() got \dontrun{} since can never run non-interactively CI. first ---cran run also caught real bug: carbon_tracker()/with_emissions_tracked() examples didn’t pass output_dir, machine codecarbon installed wrote emissions.csv check directory – fixed adding output_dir = tempdir(). Confirm Authors@R includes copyright holder role – add "cph" Beatrice Bock’s role = c(...) DESCRIPTION ’s c("aut", "cre") currently (CRAN wants explicit copyright holder, just author/maintainer). Done. Write cran-comments.md repo root (.Rbuildignore don’t want built tarball, though CRAN’s web form also asks comments directly). Cover: first submission; package one line; Python/conda point noted – codecarbon R equivalent, setup_carbon_tracker() opt-/interactive/confirmed installs isolated conda environment, never touches user’s system Python, never runs R CMD check (errors intentionally non-interactive contexts, test suite checks ). Written .Rbuildignored. R, package directory: r     usethis::use_version("minor")   # bumps 0.0.0.9000 -> 0.1.0, tags NEWS.md     devtools::check(remote = TRUE, manual = TRUE)   # full local check     devtools::check_win_devel()      # builds R's Windows dev servers, emails log     urlchecker::url_check()          # catches dead links docs/README/vignette three come back clean (0 errors, 0 warnings, ideally 0 notes) submitting. check_win_devel() particular catches things local machine’s R version won’t. Update NEWS.md’s heading # CodeCarbonR (development version) (0.0.0.9000) real version, CITATION.cff’s version:/date-released: match. Submission: devtools::submit_cran() – builds source tarball, uploads CRAN’s submission form, pulls maintainer info + cran-comments.md content form automatically. (Manual alternative: build R CMD build ., upload resulting .tar.gz cran.r-project.org/submit.html.) () CRAN emails confirmation link maintainer address DESCRIPTION – click . submission doesn’t enter queue confirmed. Wait. CRAN’s automated checks (multiple OSes/R versions) typically report back within day two; human CRAN team member reviews . Total time unpredictable – -day acceptances multi-week back--forth happen, package installing external software setup (even opt-) exactly kind thing can prompt question rather immediate accept. CRAN comes back required changes: fix , bump patch version (e.g. 0.1.0 -> 0.1.1), add line cran-comments.md “Resubmission” heading explaining changed, resubmit way. acceptance: tag/release GitHub haven’t already (Section 2 ), bump DESCRIPTION’s version new .9000 development suffix (e.g. 0.1.0.9000) ’s clear main past released version.
code: Done manually rather than via `usethis::use_version()` (version was already bumped by hand). `R CMD check --as-cran` run instead of `devtools::check(remote = TRUE, manual = TRUE)` -- equivalent package-level coverage, but note it didn't check reverse dependencies (moot for a first submission with none). `urlchecker::url_check()`: all URLs OK. `check_win_devel()` submitted 2026-08-19 09:2X; results email to beabockm@gmail.com ~15-30 min later -- **check that email and address anything it flags before submitting.**  Results email arrived 2026-08-19 18:53: 2 NOTEs, 0 warnings, 0 errors on R-devel/Windows. - "Possibly misspelled words in DESCRIPTION: conda (9:35)" -- false   positive, `conda` isn't in the spellchecker's dictionary but is a   real, correctly-spelled term. Left as-is; noted in   `cran-comments.md` so it doesn't look overlooked. - `carbon_tracker_ready()` example took 13.09s (>10s threshold) --   real issue, not a flake: on a machine with no Python configured   (like a fresh check server), `reticulate::py_module_available()`'s   interpreter discovery alone exceeds 10s before returning `FALSE`.   Fixed by wrapping the example in `\donttest{}` in `R/setup.R` and   regenerating `man/carbon_tracker_ready.Rd` via   `roxygen2::roxygenise()` (landed in commit `6eed5f3`, not `8ded4c5`   as originally logged here -- that hash was actually the unrelated   Ceres/HPC conda-discovery fix). Reverified locally with   `R CMD check --as-cran` 2026-08-19: `checking examples ... OK`,   no >5s flag. Resubmitted to `check_win_devel()` the same day   (~14:00); results email arrived ~14:08 (server-side check took   270s): **1 NOTE, 0 warnings, 0 errors** -- only the expected   "conda" spelling false-positive remains. Timing NOTE confirmed   gone on a real bare check server, not just this machine. This   item is done.

title: Create a carbon emissions tracker — carbon_tracker
text: tracker instance supports one $start()/$stop() cycle. Calling $start() $stop() instance restart measurement, codecarbon's underlying tracker never resets internal clock – exactly next $stop() returns depends installed codecarbon version: codecarbon 2.x returns first cycle's emissions/energy figures , frozen; codecarbon 3.x instead keeps accumulating energy original start, second reading comes back inflated rather frozen. Either way isolated measurement second cycle's work, duration keeps climbing original start rather resetting. measure several phases separately, create new carbon_tracker() per phase; $stop() still appends row output_dir's emissions.csv.

title: Create a carbon emissions tracker — carbon_tracker
code: # \donttest{ # Requires codecarbon to be installed (setup_carbon_tracker()); not run # on CRAN's check machines, which don't have it. if (carbon_tracker_ready()) {   tracker <- carbon_tracker(country_iso_code = "USA", output_dir = tempdir())   tracker$start()   Sys.sleep(1)   emissions <- tracker$stop()   print(emissions) } #> Downloading uv... #> Done! # }
